topic: Boutique Fitness Is Growing. We Have a Responsibility to Build Companies That Last.

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Boutique Fitness Is Growing. We Have a Responsibility to Build Companies That Last.

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Boutique fitness is seeing a whole new generation of customers coming through its doors. Boutique fitness is seeing a whole new generation of customers coming through its doors. In the first half of 2026, boutique studios led the fitness industry in year-over-year visits per location. As gym and at-home fitness options are more available than ever, more clients are seeking a boutique, in-person, communal experience. In my own Physique 57 studios, women just out of college are taking classes in numbers I haven’t seen in 20 years of running the business. Some even arrive on Saturday mornings in workout sets that match the colors of their alma mater. That is wonderful news for our industry. It also brings a responsibility: to build well-run, profitable companies that will still be here for these clients in ten, fifteen, or twenty years. I learned this firsthand as Physique 57 grew. Each new market, product, and revenue stream brought opportunities, but also placed new demands on our team, systems, and leadership. My responsibility was to make sure the company could support what the brand was promising. That meant looking beyond whether an opportunity could generate revenue and asking whether we could deliver it consistently, profitably, and with the care our clients expected. Building a powerful brand and building a company capable of supporting it are two different jobs.

en.headline: Boutique Fitness Is Growing. We Have a Responsibility to Build Companies That Last.

de.headline: Boutique Fitness Is Growing. We Have a Responsibility to Build Companies That Last.
